sections.formatNote: 1 to 3 key-takeaway bullets, each a sentence a policymaker could act on.
sections.note: The venue's bulleted summary, submitted with the abstract.
sections.title: Key Takeaways

sections.formatNote: Between 150 and 200 words (fewer is fine if everything is covered), narrative, no headings. The first one or two sentences give useful or contextual background; the next one or two say what you sought to do or did; the next one or two give the results — if there is a central quantitative finding, state it specifically; the last sentence or sentences give the policy implications or recommendations. Methods only at a very general level; no jargon; no acronyms. The abstract presents the paper in miniature: what it is about, why it matters and its relation to policy, what it adds, what it recommends.
sections.title: Abstract

sections.formatNote: No longer than 200 words: a brief promotional text that entices a reader to click through, published online in the table of contents. No citations; define any abbreviations.
sections.note: Encouraged for all article types; submitted for peer review in the main manuscript file under the heading "Teaser text", before the main text.
